raw_response:
I am old now, and on 4.1 mu I cannot do fancy things. I do mostly what has worked on my land and what the other people nearby also do. Wheat and maize together keep the land busy and give us steadier grain, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation. I have only two people at home, and cash also matters, so I will not chase very high input. But I also do not want the crop to go hungry. If I use too little fertilizer and the wheat turns yellow or the maize stays thin, then I lose more than I save. Since I have well water, I will save it for the important times and not irrigate too many times because pumping costs money.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using a local improved seed that people around here commonly buy. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then add one more round around jointing if the crop looks like it needs strength. Wheat needs water more steadily, so I will give it about 3 irrigations if rainfall is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize quickly on the same land. The gap is short, so I will keep tillage simple and not waste time. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, put a base fertilizer when planting, then topdress once when the plants are growing fast. If rain is decent, maybe one irrigation is enough, but if it turns dry I can give a second one from the well. I do not like spending much on pesticide unless I really see a problem, but I will use herbicide and maybe insecticide if needed.
